real_conflicts: Replacing the jagged fire line with a 'stylized mountain silhouette' (Visual Concept) would destroy the kinetic energy of the composition. The current zig-zag acts as a dynamic diagonal vector that cuts through the negative space; replacing it with a static, grounded shape would flatten the visual tension and make the poster feel like a generic landscape illustration rather than an urgent warning.

Rendering 'IS ENOUGH' in a 'glowing ember-orange' (Typography) would cause the headline to visually dissolve into the fire graphic. The text must remain a distinct, heavy anchor to ground the composition; if it glows, it loses its structural weight and merges with the background chaos, violating the mandate for clear focal dominance.
accepted: Realigning the headline 'ONE SPARK IS ENOUGH' to a single, strong horizontal axis (Composition) to establish a stable visual foundation. This creates a necessary counter-balance to the chaotic diagonal of the fire line.
Applying a heavy drop-shadow or stroke to the text (Typography) to separate it from the background. This ensures the typography acts as a distinct layer above the imagery, maintaining legibility.
concession: I concede that the current 'spark' element is too small and disconnected to serve as a primary focal point. It fails to anchor the visual narrative of the fire line, leaving the bottom left quadrant feeling empty and the instructional text stranded.
compromise: We will retain the jagged fire line as the primary dynamic element but 'ground' it by adding a subtle, dark mountain silhouette in the background behind the text. The headline 'ONE SPARK IS ENOUGH' will be aligned to a single horizontal axis (centered or left-aligned) and rendered in high-contrast white with a heavy drop shadow to ensure it sits clearly above the fire graphic. The 'spark' will be enlarged and positioned at the origin of the fire line to visually 'ignite' the composition, creating a clear cause-and-effect visual path.
nonnegotiable: The headline must remain a single, unified typographic block that is clearly legible against the background, acting as the primary anchor for the composition.
